claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me **how many children** you're inquiring about and **what are their names**?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm inquiring about my child Alex. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So I'm assessing eligibility for **Alex**.

To help determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to gather some details about your circumstances.

**First question: How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 20 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know Alex is 20 years old.

**Next question: Is Alex in full-time education or an approved training scheme?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I appreciate you clarifying that.

**Next question: Is Alex in paid work or self-employment?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't working at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**Next question: Are you the person with primary responsibility for Alex, and do you live with Alex in the same household?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home and I'm responsible for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

**Next question: What is your current residency status in the UK? For example, are you a British citizen, settled status holder, or do you have another immigration status?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I live in the UK - I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**Next question: Are you currently receiving any of the following benefits: Income Support, income-based Jobseeker's Allowance, income-related Employment and Support Allowance, or Pension Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not receiving any of those benefits.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

**Next question: What is your approximate annual household income, or are you receiving Working Tax Credit or Child Tax Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not receiving Working Tax Credit or Child Tax Credit. Why do you need to know about my income though? I thought I was just checking if I'm eligible for Child Benefit?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's a great question, and I apologize if that wasn't clear! You're right to ask.

Child Benefit eligibility is primarily based on **who the child is and your relationship to them** — not on your income level. The main factors are things like the child's age, whether they're in education or training, and whether you're their primary carer living with them.

I was asking about income because it can be relevant to understanding your overall circumstances, but you're correct that it's not a determining factor for Child Benefit eligibility itself.

Based on what you've told me so far, let me check: **Is Alex a British citizen or do they have settled status in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

I have one more question to complete my assessment:

**Have there been any changes to Alex's circumstances in the last few weeks — for example, have they recently left education, started or stopped work, or moved out of your home?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, there haven't been any recent changes. Alex has been at home with me and not in education or work for a while now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I now have all the details I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the information you've provided, I'm able to make a determination:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Result: You are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

**Why?** Child Benefit can be claimed for children up to age 16. This age limit can be extended to 19 if the child is in full-time education or an approved training scheme. However, Alex is 20 years old and is not currently in education, training, or work, so they fall outside the eligible age range.

If Alex's circumstances change — for example, if they enter full-time education or training before their 20th birthday — the eligibility position could be different, but based on their current situation at age 20, they do not qualify.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
